objectives: Trace ed-tech from Skinner's teaching machine to modern ITS + Khan Academy.
Evaluate the MOOC era + Reich's Failure to Disrupt thesis.
Survey adaptive systems + learning analytics + standards (xAPI, Caliper).

slides.title: A century of educational technology
slides.body:
**Pre-digital**:
- **Sidney Pressey** (1924): teaching + testing machine for multiple-choice items; never widely adopted.
- **B.F. Skinner** (1958 Harvard Educational Review 'Teaching Machines'): mechanical device presenting linear programmed instruction with immediate reinforcement. Directly motivated by his operant theory of learning. Predicted: '... there will be in any large school more such machines than there are teachers.' Did not happen — but the lineage is direct from Skinner to CAI to ITS to modern adaptive systems.
- **Norman Crowder** (1959): **branched programmed instruction** — adapt the next item based on the learner's response, an early adaptive system.

**PLATO** (Programmed Logic for Automated Teaching Operations; University of Illinois 1960, scaling through the 1970s under Bitzer + colleagues): the first large-scale computer-based education system. Custom hardware (the PLATO IV terminal with orange plasma display, 1972), the TUTOR programming language, lessons across hundreds of subjects, multi-user simulations, message boards, email, instant messaging, + multiplayer games (Empire, Avatar, dnd, MUDs avant la lettre). Influenced essentially everything that came after. Control Data Corporation commercialized it.

**CAI + microcomputer era (1970s-1990s)**: BASIC drill-and-practice; Apple II + IBM PC in classrooms; Logo turtle graphics (Papert; Mindstorms 1980); Reader Rabbit, Math Blaster, Oregon Trail. CD-ROM era: Encarta, Magic School Bus.

**Intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)**: combine domain model + student model + tutor model + interface.
- **Anderson, Corbett, Koedinger** (CMU; ACT-R cognitive architecture; Cognitive Tutor 1990s+; later Carnegie Learning): rule-based cognitive models, knowledge tracing (Bayesian Knowledge Tracing — Corbett + Anderson 1995), Hint + worked-example scaffolds. The Algebra Cognitive Tutor showed Pittsburgh-area gains of ~1σ in some studies. Foundational lineage.
- **Andes Physics Tutor** (VanLehn + colleagues).
- **AutoTutor, GuruTutor** (Graesser): dialogue-based tutors.

**Khan Academy** (Salman Khan 2006 YouTube videos for his cousin; non-profit 2008): free videos + practice + mastery system; tens of millions of users; the original 'flip-the-classroom' kit. Subsequent expansion into Khan Academy Kids, MAP-aligned practice, Khanmigo (LLM tutor) 2023.

**Carpe Diem schools** (Rick Ogston, Arizona 2006): rotational blended-learning model — students rotate between online instruction + small-group tutoring + project work; influenced K-12 blended-learning charter network design (Rocketship, Summit Public Schools).

**Bloom's 2-sigma problem** (Benjamin Bloom 1984): one-to-one mastery tutoring produces ~2σ gains over traditional classrooms. The implicit challenge: can we approximate this at scale through systems? ITS + adaptive + AI-tutor research has been chasing this benchmark for 40 years.

slides.title: The MOOC era + online learning
slides.body:
**The MOOC moment (2011-2012)**:
- **Stanford's free AI class** (Sebastian Thrun + Peter Norvig fall 2011): ~160,000 enrolees; surprise scale.
- **Coursera** (Andrew Ng + Daphne Koller, 2012); **edX** (MIT + Harvard, 2012); **Udacity** (Thrun, 2012); **FutureLearn** (UK, 2013); **XuetangX** (China, 2013).
- The New York Times declared 2012 'The Year of the MOOC.' Hype peak: prediction that traditional universities would be disrupted.

**The cold shower (2013-2017)**:
- **Completion rates**: typically 5-15% across surveyed MOOCs (Reich + Ruipérez-Valiente 2019 Science 'The MOOC pivot'). Highly self-selected learners.
- **Audience**: predominantly already-educated adults from wealthy countries — not the underserved that hype promised.
- **Pivots**: edX + Coursera moved toward paid certificates, MicroMasters, online degrees (Georgia Tech OMSCS 2014 was an early model; ~tenth the cost of on-campus); Udacity pivoted to Nanodegrees + corporate training; Thrun famously said in 2013 'we have a lousy product.'

**Justin Reich Failure to Disrupt: Why Technology Alone Can't Transform Education (2020)**: thesis — technology repeatedly amplifies existing inequities rather than disrupting them. New learning tech benefits learners who already have time, skills, support, broadband. To improve outcomes for underserved learners, design must address human supports + structural conditions, not just deliver content at scale. A measured + research-grounded counter to the prior hype cycle.

**Flipped + blended learning** (Bergmann + Sams 2007/2012; Christensen + Horn 2008 Disrupting Class): direct instruction (video, reading) outside class; problem-solving + discussion + practice in class. Modest but real gains when paired with active in-class engagement (Freeman et al. 2014).

**Blended-learning models** (Christensen + Horn Blended 2014): station-rotation, lab-rotation, flipped, individual-rotation, flex, A La Carte, enriched virtual. Charter networks (Summit, Rocketship, Carpe Diem, KIPP) implemented variants.

**Pandemic acceleration (2020-2022)**: emergency remote teaching at planetary scale exposed both the potential + limits of online + remote learning, particularly for younger + disadvantaged learners. Substantial learning loss (NWEA, NAEP, World Bank reports); ed-tech investment surge + subsequent contraction. Effective practices: Zoom + LMS + low-bandwidth options + paper-based supports + community check-ins; weak practices: synchronous lecture-only + ignoring student access conditions.

**Modern online + microcredentials**:
- **Coursera + edX + Udacity** moved upmarket into degrees + corporate.
- **2U / edX** acquisition (2021); subsequent strain.
- **Industry certificates** (Google Career Certificates, AWS, Meta) increasingly recognized.
- **Bootcamps**: General Assembly, Flatiron, Lambda School (Bloom Institute of Technology) — mixed outcomes; ISA controversies.
- **K-12 online**: Florida Virtual School, K12 Inc / Stride, Connections Academy.
- **Open educational resources (OER)**: MERLOT, OpenStax, OER Commons, CK-12; Creative Commons licensed.

slides.title: Adaptive systems + learning analytics + standards
slides.body:
**Adaptive learning systems**:
- **Knewton** (founded 2008; acquired by Wiley 2019): adaptive platform integrated with publisher textbooks; Bayesian knowledge tracing + recommendation. Mixed evidence; significant business pivots.
- **ALEKS** (Assessment + Learning in Knowledge Spaces; Falmagne + Doignon knowledge-space theory; McGraw-Hill): a learning-graph + adaptive assessment system widely used in higher-ed math. Strong empirical track record in some studies.
- **DreamBox, i-Ready, MAP Growth (NWEA), iXL**: K-12 adaptive math + literacy systems.
- **DragonBox** (Wewer Knudsen 2012+; later acquired by Kahoot): puzzle-game-based math learning (algebra, fractions, geometry); strong concept-acquisition results.
- **Duolingo**: half-life-regression adaptive scheduling (Settles + Meeder 2016) + course-construction at scale.
- **Squirrel AI** (China 2014+): nano-skill knowledge graph + adaptive tutoring; large field trials.
- **AlphaCode + LLM-based tutors** are now reshaping the adaptive space (next lesson).

**Learning Management Systems**: Blackboard (1997), Moodle (2002), Canvas / Instructure (2008-), Schoology, Brightspace, Google Classroom (2014). Most large institutions run a primary LMS + several specialty tools.

**Data dashboards + early-warning systems**: Civitas Learning, Purdue's Course Signals, Georgia State's Predictive Analytics + retention work (Renick) — credited with closing graduation gaps. Risk: surveillance + label effects.

**Standards for learning data**:
- **SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model, 1999, ADL)**: package + sequence + track e-learning content; legacy but still ubiquitous.
- **xAPI (Experience API / Tin Can, 2013, ADL)**: actor-verb-object statements about learning activity stored in a **Learning Record Store (LRS)**; far richer than SCORM completion status.
- **IMS Caliper Analytics (2015)**: standardized event vocabularies + sensor model; complementary to xAPI.
- **LTI (Learning Tools Interoperability, IMS Global)**: standard for embedding tools in LMSes.
- **OneRoster + CASE**: rostering + competency frameworks.

**Learning analytics + educational data mining**:
- **George Siemens + Stephen Downes** + the **connectivism** movement (~2005): learning theory for digital + networked age; framed early LAK + MOOCs. Siemens organized the first Learning Analytics + Knowledge (LAK) conference (2011). Society for Learning Analytics Research (SoLAR).
- **Educational Data Mining (EDM) society** (~2008): more ML-leaning sibling community.
- Techniques: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (Corbett + Anderson 1995), Performance Factors Analysis (Pavlik), Deep Knowledge Tracing (Piech 2015 NIPS) + later self-attentive variants, sequence models, item-response IRT, latent skill models, transformers over learning sequences.
- **Privacy + ethics**: FERPA (US), GDPR (EU); data minimization; learner control; algorithmic-fairness audits; the surveillance-capitalism critique (Williamson Big Data in Education 2017).

**Mobile + microlearning**: Duolingo + Quizlet + Anki + Memrise + Brilliant + Sololearn — bite-size, mobile, spaced, adaptive. Mobile-first is increasingly the norm in emerging markets (Eneza, Ubongo, M-Shule, BYJU'S, Unacademy, Toppr, Vedantu, Yuanfudao, MasterClass, Outlier.org).

**Where this lands**: a deep + uneven infrastructure for tracking + adapting to learners exists today. Whether it produces durable, equitable learning depends on instructional design + human supports + governance — Reich's central point.

question.question: Trace ITS lineage to a modern tutor
question.goal: A start-up is building an LLM-based algebra tutor. Map their plan onto the ITS lineage from Anderson-Corbett-Koedinger to today.

steps.prompt: What were the four components of a classical ITS?

acceptedAnswers: domain model; student model; tutor model; user interface

steps.reveal: Classical ITS architecture: (1) domain model — what is to be learned; (2) student model — what the learner knows + their misconceptions; (3) tutor / pedagogical model — what to do next; (4) user interface. Anderson + Corbett + Koedinger Cognitive Tutor + ACT-R is the canonical instantiation.

steps.prompt: What is Bayesian Knowledge Tracing + who proposed it?

acceptedAnswers: Corbett + Anderson 1995; HMM tracking mastery per knowledge component

steps.reveal: BKT (Corbett + Anderson 1995): a 2-state hidden-Markov model per knowledge component — known vs unknown — with parameters for prior learning, learning rate, slip + guess. Provides a per-skill mastery probability + drives hint + practice decisions in Cognitive Tutor + many ITS systems.

steps.prompt: How might an LLM tutor strengthen the domain + tutor model?

acceptedAnswers: natural-language explanation + hint generation; flexible dialogue; open-ended scaffolding

hints: What can LLMs do that rule-based systems struggled with?
steps.reveal: LLMs offer flexible natural-language explanation + hint generation + open-ended dialogue + adaptive scaffolding that rule-based systems struggled with. The domain model can be substituted or augmented by retrieval from textbooks; the tutor model can produce Socratic moves on the fly.

steps.prompt: What classical-ITS strengths must the team preserve?

acceptedAnswers: calibrated student model; mastery + practice scheduling; correctness guarantees; instructional alignment + evaluation

hints: Where LLMs are weak: hallucination, calibration, scheduling, evaluation.
steps.reveal: Preserve: a calibrated student model (knowledge tracing or successor); explicit mastery + practice scheduling (Bjork desirable difficulties + SRS); correctness guarantees on math (symbolic checker or unit tests around LLM); curriculum + instructional alignment + evidence-based evaluation. LLMs hallucinate, miscalibrate, + drift; the classical ITS scaffolding addresses exactly these. The state of the art combines LLMs with knowledge tracing + symbolic checks.

question.question: What is the central thesis of Justin Reich's Failure to Disrupt (2020)?
options: Technology will inevitably disrupt all education.

Educational technology repeatedly amplifies existing inequities rather than disrupting them. New systems tend to benefit learners who already have time, skills, support, + broadband; durable improvement for underserved learners requires human supports + structural change, not just scaled content. Reich draws on MOOC completion data (~5-15% completion; predominantly already-educated adults from wealthy countries — Reich + Ruipérez-Valiente 2019 Science) + decades of ed-tech adoption patterns. A measured, evidence-grounded counter to disruption hype.
Free content delivery solves all access problems.
question.explanation: Reich Failure to Disrupt 2020: ed-tech amplifies existing inequities. MOOC completion ~5-15% with already-educated audiences. Durable improvement requires human supports + structural change, not just content at scale.

slides.workedSolution: Justin Reich 2020 Failure to Disrupt: ed-tech repeatedly amplifies existing inequities; MOOC completion ~5-15% (Reich + Ruipérez-Valiente 2019 Science) + audience skews already-educated + wealthy. Durable improvement needs human supports + structural change, not just scaled content.

question.question: Choosing data standards for a new district platform
question.prompt: You are advising a US school district building a new analytics platform across LMS + adaptive tools + assessments. Recommend a stack covering xAPI vs Caliper, LTI integration, a learning-record store, dashboards, privacy controls (FERPA), + how the design responds to Williamson-style + Reich-style critiques.

question.question: MOOC engagement: of 160,000 enrolees in Thrun + Norvig's 2011 Stanford AI class, ~23,000 finished. Approximate completion rate (%)?

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, sketch the lineage from Skinner's teaching machine to modern adaptive learning systems.
question.rubric: Mentions: Skinner's 1958 teaching machine operationalized programmed instruction + immediate reinforcement; Crowder added branching. PLATO (Illinois 1960s) brought CAI to scale + invented many networked-learning primitives. The 1980s-90s saw microcomputers + CAI + the rise of intelligent tutoring systems — Anderson, Corbett, Koedinger's Cognitive Tutor with Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (Corbett + Anderson 1995) at CMU. Khan Academy (Salman Khan 2006) brought free mastery practice to scale; Carpe Diem + Summit modelled blended learning. Knewton, ALEKS, DreamBox, DragonBox, Squirrel AI, Duolingo (half-life regression, Settles + Meeder 2016) developed adaptive scheduling. Data standards (xAPI, Caliper) + learning analytics (Siemens, BKT → Deep Knowledge Tracing) enable measurement. Today: LLM-based tutors stand on this 60-year stack — combining flexible dialogue with calibrated knowledge tracing + mastery scheduling + evaluation, with Reich's caution that scale alone does not solve equity.
